_comment: Tier-2 for skfem adaptive_poisson#4, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: 'Dorfler / max-strategy marking with theta=0.5 is the standard sweet spot -- theta -> 1 gives near-uniform refinement, theta -> 0 gives 1-element-at-a-time', with healthy convergence showing N growing 1.3-2x per step and max_eta dropping 30-50%. Ran: L-shape MeshTri.init_lshaped().refined(3) (384 elements, 225 DOFs) with the exact r^(2/3) datum, an interior-facet gradient-jump indicator, both marking rules evaluated on the SAME indicator field at theta = 0.1/0.5/0.9, their limits, and a seven-step Dorfler loop at theta = 0.5. Printed: THE ENTRY NAMES TWO STRATEGIES WHOSE theta RUNS IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. Dorfler marks 1/2/18 elements as theta rises; the max-strategy marks 26/4/1. In the limits Dorfler goes from 1 element to all 384 while the max-strategy goes from all 384 to none. So 'Dorfler / max-strategy with theta = 0.5' does not name a setting, and a reader implementing the max-strategy from that sentence gets near-uniform refinement exactly where they were told to expect one element at a time. The DOF rule of thumb also fails here: a real theta = 0.5 Dorfler loop grows N by 1.11-1.16x per step, well under the quoted 1.3-2x, and max_eta does not drop at all. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 applies the documented fix inside max_strategy -- the threshold is complemented, eta_K > (1 - theta) * max eta, so the max-strategy's theta finally runs the same way round as Dorfler's. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 12 expect_in_output strings; the max-strategy counts flip from 26/4/1 to 1/4/26, removing 'max_strategy_marks_fewer_as_theta_rises=True', 'the_two_conventions_run_in_opposite_directions=True', 'max_theta_tiny_is_everything=True' and 'max_theta_one_is_nothing=True', and firing the forbidden 'FAIL:', so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
